subject: riotInterceptor
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: corporate riot-control interceptor with a water cannon and neon light bars.
Style: Cyberpunk 2077.
reasoning:
I'm planning the vehicle design as a static armored riot-control interceptor, around 5.2m long and 2.4m wide, facing +Z, with big wheels, a roof-mounted water cannon turret, neon light bars, and corporate logo decals.

Since no joints are needed for a static model, I'll use simple box and cylinder helper functions, a glow kit import, and invented textures like a "KIRO-TEC" logo and hazard stripes. I'm now laying out the chassis geometry piece by piece—underbody, lower body, and sloped hood—positioning each box at the right height so the wheels sit correctly on the ground.

Still working out the hood and cabin shapes...

Still shaping body profiles...

I'm adding a roof light bar with alternating magenta/blue glow near the front, then working out the windshield as an angled plane fitted to the cabin's slope, computing its normal direction and placement offset to sit flush against the roof-to-front slope.

Now I'm working out the wheel layout—three axles with large radius tires, dark rubber tread cylinders, metal hubs, and a glowing neon torus ring accent, positioned at the outer x edges of the chassis.

Shaping the plow wedge profile and giving it a yellow/black diagonal hazard stripe pattern for that cyberpunk look, then moving on to the front fascia with grille and headlights at the body's front face.

Working out the hood slope geometry and placing a glowing cyan headlight bar across the front, with angled "eye slash" accents at the ends for an aggressive look.

I'm positioning the grille texture lower on the front face, but realize it conflicts with the plow's z-range, so I need to shrink the plow lower to avoid the overlap.

Rather than fitting a small grille, I'll skip it and place a logo decal on the hood instead, computing the hood's slope normal to properly orient the flat plane against the angled surface.

I'm working through the orientation so the logo texture reads upright when viewed from the front, flipping the up-axis to account for the hood sloping toward the rear. I'm also planning to add glowing neon strips along the hood edges for extra detail.

Now I'm positioning additional neon accents: magenta light bars along the lower body sides, plus a cyan underglow strip running beneath the chassis.

I'll go with 4 chunky wheels instead, positioning them to leave room for an 1.8-long side decal between the arches. For the decal plane facing outward, I need to work out the correct orientation so the text reads properly when viewed from the side, considering the car's front-back axis relative to the viewer's perspective.

Now I'm adding the roof light bar with alternating red/blue glow boxes.

Still designing roof details... then I'm building a cage grill over the windshield using thin rods positioned along the slope, mixing slanted and horizontal bars for structure, before starting on the turret base cylinder.

Now I'm defining the turret body sitting on its swivel base, with a barrel rod aimed slightly upward and a flared nozzle at the tip resembling a water-cannon bell. I'm working out the barrel's direction vector and endpoint to position collar rings along its length.

For the nozzle, I want a glowing cyan disc facing outward at the tip, and I'm considering adding a pressure gauge on the turret's side -- deciding to skip the kit's gauge texture and draw a custom HUD-style gauge instead. I also need to figure out a curved hose connecting the tank top to the rear of the turret, working out the coordinates for both ends.

Now I'm positioning the hose's arc with a midpoint, then shaping the tank itself as a cylinder oriented along the z-axis with capped ends, sized to rest properly on top of the lower body.

Adding tank straps as dark rings at the top and bottom of the tank, plus a hexagon logo decal on the sides. For the rear, I'm considering exhaust pipes positioned vertically near the cabin's back corners.

Now I'm placing exhaust stacks with glowing orange tips above the cabin, mirror arms at the cabin front sides, door handle and door line details, and an antenna. I'm also adding roof-mounted spotlights positioned to avoid conflicting with the light bar, and sketching in bull bars and skid plate rods connecting the front plow to the headlights.

Adding chassis axle rods...

Writing wheel and hub details...

Rather than baking unique paint per wheel, I'll go simpler with a generic paint factory keyed on wheel center position so I can reuse one function across all four wheels. Now I'm planning the full texture set needed: a corporate logo emblem, side unit lettering, headlight slit, windshield, side window, gauge cluster, and possibly a rear grille or ad board panel.

Thinking through LED signage placement: an amber "STAND DOWN" strip on the rear tank face, plus a front sign board mounted above the windshield near the roof's front edge, positioning it carefully so it doesn't collide with the roof light bar or turret.

Confirming the barrel clears the sign height-wise. For the color palette, I'm going cyberpunk: dark gunmetal body with magenta, cyan, yellow, and red accents, applying a mottled countershade paint with subtle panel noise and rivets for texture on the body material.

Now I'm figuring out the livery details — adding a hazard-stripe pattern (alternating yellow-black) along the lower body skirt where the body normal faces sideways and the height falls in the skirt range, giving a hazard-tape look, then starting on a different panel treatment for the cabin.

Still defining the extrusion outlines for the cabin, lower body, and plow, setting their profile points in (z,y) coordinates with appropriate thickness and bevel so the shapes extrude correctly along the origin point.

I'm now adding bull bars as rods extending from the plow, plus working out the headlight placement by calculating the normal vector of the hood's front slope to position the eye planes correctly against that angled surface.

Then I'm sizing the headlight eyes and adding a glow strip between them, double-checking the plow's clearance against the eye height so nothing overlaps. After that I'm adding roof ribs, a hatch panel, a side mirror arm, and vertical trim lines on the cabin doors for extra detail.

I'll skip detailed doors since the windows read fine, just adding small door handles. For unique flair I'm considering riot shield racks or shield plates on the tank sides but deciding to skip the complex curved geometry in favor of a simpler look, then adding a rear ladder, a dark rear bumper box, and vertical taillight bars positioned against the rear body face.

Now I'm placing glowing red taillight boxes near the tank's flat rear cap, adding a rear sign plane oriented to face backward correctly, and planning a roof-mounted sensor dome plus a camera pod with a glowing red lens on the turret. Mesh count looks fine, so I'm moving to writing the actual helper functions.

Writing box helper...

Now I'm designing the SVG textures: a hexagonal logo with a stylized "K" and bolt in yellow/black for "KIRO·TEC", and a side panel with "CROWD SUPPRESSION" text, a yellow bar, and unit labeling, avoiding characters that might not render.

Still writing SVG code...

Also figuring out the tank's decal placement, working out the cylinder face geometry to position the side logos without them floating off the surface, settling on a slight offset along x to keep them flush.

That edge gap seems too large, so I'm shrinking the logo to .4 and considering decaling it directly onto the tank surface instead, since the tank is a proper Part. For the lower body sides and hood, I'm checking that the flat bevel faces let a plane sit close enough to the surface at those slanted points.

Still working out the hood decal's position and tilt, computing the normal and setting a local up vector so it leans correctly against the slope. For the hood vents I'm considering small glow slits but may skip them since the neon strips already cover that area well enough, then moving on to the cabin's hex armor detailing on the sides.

Now I'm looping through the four wheel positions and writing the tire geometry and paint logic -- using angle-based texturing to differentiate the flat side faces from the tread blocks, then starting on the hub cylinder's dimensions and steel coloring.

Adding wheel hub details...

Then I'm placing fender boxes above each wheel as flared black guards that extend beyond the body's edge, giving the car a flared-wheel-arch look.

I'm also planning red and blue siren boxes with glowing covers and black frames for the top of the vehicle.

Next I'm positioning searchlights with cylindrical bodies and glowing front discs near the roof, plus an antenna rod at the back of the cabin roof with a small glowing red tip.

I'm also placing underbody neon strips in cyan near the lower body edges, along with side neon bars near the skirt line, carefully coordinating their heights and z-depth ranges so they don't clash with existing decals, hazard paint, or wheel fenders.

Checking the side neon positions, I realize they'd actually intersect the wheels, so I need to split them into segments that fit cleanly between the wheel wells, computing the gap based on the front and rear wheel z-ranges and sizing the magenta bar and side decal to fit that middle space.

I'm also sketching a cyan rod along the cabin roof edge and a frame rod across the windshield top, plus skipping some minor fender light details as unnecessary, then setting up normal vector constants for the windshield slope before writing the full geometry code.

Still placing the cage rods and crossbars along the windshield slope, then starting to position the side window planes relative to the cabin profile's y-extent.

Now I'm sketching the turret base cylinder and its position above the cabin roof.

Working through the neon ring, cannon body box, and barrel geometry: setting a pivot point, computing a direction vector for the barrel, and placing the shroud and barrel cylinders along that axis with appropriate radii and lengths.

Still placing barrel segments, bands, nozzle flare, and a glowing tip disc oriented along the barrel direction, then starting the hose connector running from the tank to the turret rear.

Camera lens uses a small circle for the red glow. I'm also finalizing the turret hatch, tail pipe, roof LED sign and sirens, double-checking wheel radius so the model's lowest point sits exactly at y=0, and adding a hazard checkerboard paint pattern across the plow and skirt.

Lower body paint applies hazard stripes near the wheel wells and the panelled body texture elsewhere, confirming the kit imports and countershading helper work correctly before I start writing the rod placement code.
